findings.title: getCredentials dereferences a possibly-null MyUser
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` returns null when the user is not in the `users` map, for example after removal or for a user from another provider instance. `getCredentials` then calls `myUser.recoveryCodes` without a null check. Every other method (`isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`) guards against null. A missing user would cause an NPE during credential listing instead of an empty stream.

findings.title: Used-up user-storage codes are never removed, and used codes are not tracked
findings.body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential from user storage. The following lines still call `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())` when `allCodesUsed()`. That call only removes credentials in the local DB. The federated credential is not removed, and its id may be null, as it is for the test storage model built via `createFromValues`.

Nothing marks a code as used when it is validated against user storage either. `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` normally does that on validation, but the user-storage path bypasses it. As a result, the 'next code' shown by `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` never advances, and the used-up/re-configure logic only works for local credentials.

findings.title: Recovery-key test covers only the happy path with code 0
disableCredentialType ignores recovery codes
findings.body: The storage now supports and stores recovery codes. `disableCredentialType` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` handle only OTP, so recovery codes can never be removed or disabled through the admin API. `isConfiguredFor` keeps returning true after the admin tries to disable them, and the state leaks between tests because the factory map is shared.
